jobs.title: Deputy Director of Homeless Services*
jobs.description:
**The Job**
-----------


The **Office of Homeless Services (OHS)**is recruiting for a **Deputy Director of Homeless Services\*** who serves as a key executive leader within the department, responsible for overseeing financial management, administrative operations, strategic planning, and cross\-sector partnerships that advance housing\-focused initiatives. This role ensures effective stewardship of diverse funding streams; leads core administrative functions; and supports the implementation of programs aligned with best practices, including Housing First and evidence\-based homeless system strategies.  

***Key Responsibilities include:***  

  

**Financial Management \& Grant Administration*** Oversee complex departmental budgets and financial operations.
* Manage multiple funding streams, including federal, state, and local sources (such as HUD, HCD, and CoC\-funded programs).
* Ensure compliance with grant requirements, regulatory standards, and fiscal reporting obligations.
* Implement systems to track expenditures, monitor fiscal performance, and forecast financial needs.

**Contracting \& Procurement*** Develop and manage contracts with nonprofit service providers, consultants, and vendors.
* Oversee procurement processes in alignment with county, state, and federal rules.
* Monitor contractor performance, ensuring contractual obligations and outcomes are met.

**Strategic Operations \& Administration*** Lead administrative operations, including HR coordination, IT needs, facilities support, and general administrative systems.
* Drive process improvements to strengthen efficiency, compliance, and internal controls.
* Support departmentwide strategic planning and operational alignment.
* Manages, organizes and supervises the issuance, review and recommendation of requests for proposal/qualification for development, consultants or programs; supervises invitation for bids, inspection of properties, and other related activities; analyze programs or projects for feasibility and cost effectiveness.

**Homeless Systems Knowledge*** Apply expertise in homeless service delivery models, including Coordinated Entry Systems, HMIS, permanent supportive housing, and Housing First principles.
* Provide leadership that aligns fiscal and administrative functions with best\-practice homelessness interventions.

**Stakeholder Engagement \& Collaboration*** Build and maintain partnerships with government agencies, nonprofit providers, community groups, and other system stakeholders.
* Represent the Office of Homeless Services in regional workgroups, planning efforts, and cross\-jurisdictional initiatives.

**Data\-Driven Leadership*** Use data to evaluate program performance, fiscal stability, and operational efficiency.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement grounded in measurable outcomes.

**Staff Oversight \& Performance Management*** Supervise fiscal, administrative, and operational staff.
* Establish performance goals and ensure deliverables are met.
* Provide guidance, coaching, and professional development opportunities.
* Manages, supervises and performs routine tasks related to projects and programs; supervises and motivates staff in the development and implementation of such projects and programs; monitors progress and makes recommendations for improvements.

**Communication \& Reporting*** Present complex financial, administrative, and operational information to county leadership, elected officials, community partners, and the public.

jobs.title: New Ulm Area Foundation Executive Director
jobs.description:
**Executive Director (Part\-Time)**

**New Ulm Area Foundation, Inc. (NUAF)** is seeking a **part\-time Executive Director** to support and advance its mission. This flexible, in\-office position averages 20–30 hours per week. Compensation based on experience; no benefits are included.

**About the New Ulm Area Foundation**

New Ulm Area Foundation is a nonprofit organization whose mission is:  
*“We inspire engagement through generosity and collaboration that creates sustainable impact in the New Ulm area.”*

Our vision is:  
*“To create a flourishing community in which future generations thrive.”*

NUAF supports the community by providing grants to qualified 501(c)(3\) organizations whose work aligns with our four grantmaking pillars: Arts, Education, Historic Preservation, and Community Enhancement.

**Position Overview**

The Executive Director is responsible for the overall administration and coordination of the Foundation’s operations. This role works closely with the Board of Directors, committees, donors, and community partners to advance NUAF’s mission and ensure effective stewardship of resources.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide general office administration and organizational support
* Lead fundraising and development efforts, including donor cultivation and solicitation, and stewardship
* Manage donor relations and community engagement
* Work closely with the Board of Directors and Board committees
* Coordinate communications, including a semi\-annual newsletter, press releases, and presentations
* Facilitate administrative processes related to grantmaking, including application support, tracking, and reporting
* Serve as a visible and collaborative representative of the Foundation in the community
* Maintain accurate financial records by entering, categorizing, and reconciling transactions in QuickBooks on a regular basis

· Provide financial oversight, including budgeting, investment coordination, and grant allocation determination.

**Qualifications**

* Experience in nonprofit administration, fundraising, development, or a related field preferred
* Strong organizational, communication, and relationship\-building skills
* Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with volunteers and board members
* Passion for community impact and alignment with NUAF’s mission and values

**How to Apply**

* Send resume to apply.newulmareafoundation@gmail.com
* Applications will be accepted until the position is filled

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Lead a Mission. Strengthen a Community. Change Lives.

Springfield Family Center, Inc. is seeking an experienced, compassionate, and visionary Executive Director to lead one of the region's most important charitable organizations.

For more than 50 years, Springfield Family Center has worked alongside community partners to combat food insecurity and provide essential resources to individuals and families throughout the greater Springfield area. Through food distribution, community meals, outreach programs, advocacy, and partnerships, we help ensure that our neighbors have access to nutritious food and supportive services.

We are looking for a dynamic leader who is passionate about community impact and ready to guide our organization into its next chapter of growth and sustainability.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Springfield Family Center and is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, fundraising, financial management, community relations, and daily operations of the organization.

The Executive Director will work collaboratively with staff, volunteers, donors, community partners, and local leaders to advance our mission and strengthen our impact throughout the region.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership

* Provide strategic leadership and vision to advance the mission and goals of Springfield Family Center.
* Foster a positive, collaborative, and mission\-driven organizational culture.
* Lead organizational planning and continuous improvement efforts.
* Serve as the primary spokesperson and ambassador for the organization.

Fundraising \& Resource Development

* Develop and implement fundraising strategies to support organizational sustainability.
* Cultivate relationships with donors, foundations, corporations, and community partners.
* Oversee grant writing, grant management, and reporting requirements.
* Identify new funding opportunities and revenue streams.

Financial \& Operational Management

* Manage organizational budgets and financial resources responsibly.
* Ensure compliance with nonprofit regulations, grant requirements, and organizational policies.
* Oversee program operations, including food distribution, community meals, outreach efforts, and volunteer engagement.
* Monitor program outcomes and implement improvements when needed.

Staff Leadership

* Recruit, supervise, mentor, and support staff members.
* Promote professional development and team collaboration.
* Build and maintain a positive workplace culture.

Board \& Community Relations

* Partner closely with the Board of Directors to achieve strategic priorities.
* Provide regular updates regarding organizational performance, finances, and opportunities.
* Strengthen community partnerships and represent Springfield Family Center at public events and meetings.
* Advocate for food security and community well\-being throughout the region.

Qualifications

Required

* Demonstrated success in fundraising, grant development, and donor relations.
* Experience managing budgets and organizational finances.
* Strong supervisory and team leadership experience.
* Excellent communication, relationship\-building, and public speaking skills.

Preferred

* Master's degree in a related field or bachelor’s degree in nonprofit management, business administration, public administration, social services, or a related field.
* Experience in nonprofit leadership.
* Knowledge of food insecurity, hunger relief programs, and community services.
* Experience working with boards of directors and volunteers.

What We Offer

* Opportunity to lead a respected and impactful nonprofit organization.
* Meaningful work that directly improves lives within the community.
* Collaborative Board, staff, and volunteer support.
* Competitive compensation commensurate with experience.
* Professional growth and leadership opportunities.

Submit the following via email

* Cover Letter
* Resume
* Three Professional Reference

Springfield Family Center, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer and encourages applicants from diverse backgrounds and experiences to apply.

Pay: $50,000\.00 \- $80,000\.00 per year

People with a criminal record are encouraged to apply

Work Location: In person

jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Program DirectorKey to Kinship Family Recovery Housing Voucher Program

**Kingdom Living Iowa (dba RISE Recovery Center) — Des Moines, IA**

**Location:**

Kingdom Living Iowa, 3120 SW 9th St, Des Moines, IA (on\-site)

**Reports to**

Executive Team / Co\-Founders

**Status**

Full\-time, exempt

**Compensation**

Competitive salary and benefits, commensurate with experience *(see note at end)*

**Anticipated start**

Immediate

About Kingdom Living Iowa \& RISE Recovery Center

Kingdom Living Iowa is a Polk County–based 501(c)(3\) nonprofit that has served Iowans in recovery since 2016\. We operate one of central Iowa's largest networks of recovery housing — 15 recovery residences — alongside RISE Recovery Center, a community hub offering peer recovery support, clinical care coordination, employment and family programming, and connection to every pathway to recovery. We welcome residents on medications for opioid use disorder (MOUD) and are committed to keeping families together and honoring the dignity of every person in recovery.

About the Position

The Program Director leads **Key to Kinship**, a new family recovery housing initiative funded through Iowa HHS Opioid Settlement Funding. The program provides 30–90 day recovery housing vouchers and wraparound supports to families impacted by opioid use disorder (OUD) — with priority for pregnant and postpartum women with OUD and parents in recovery pursuing reunification with their children.

As the program's single dedicated leader, the Program Director runs the voucher program end to end: intake and eligibility, placement into MOUD\-supportive recovery housing, coordination of family supports, partner and case coordination, and full grant compliance and reporting. This is a hands\-on, mission\-critical role central to launching the program on time and to keeping Polk County families housed, stable, and connected to care.

Key Responsibilities

**Voucher Administration \& Finance**

* Oversee the recovery housing voucher system end to end, from referral through voucher exit.
* Manage the allocation and disbursement of funds for vouchers and secondary supports (transportation, infant and child necessities, employment coaching, family programming).
* Maintain a centralized financial ledger with quarterly compliance reconciliation.
* Monitor voucher utilization against the budget and adjust intake pacing to keep the program on track.

**Intake, Eligibility \& Clinical Coordination**

* Conduct intake screening, confirming OUD diagnosis or documented history of opioid use per grant eligibility requirements.
* Coordinate on\-site OUD/SUD clinical assessment and MOUD initiation or continuation through the clinical partnership with UCS Healthcare.
* Ensure naloxone (OORM) distribution and overdose\-recognition/response training for every participant and household at intake.

**Family Support Coordination**

* Coordinate delivery of wraparound supports that stabilize the whole family — transportation, infant/child necessities, employment coaching, and family programming through RISE Recovery Center.
* Conduct family needs assessments and lead quarterly case reviews with partners.
* Support custody and reunification milestones in coordination with Iowa HHS Division of Children and Family Services (DCFS) and the family court system.

**Strategic Partnerships \& Referrals**

* Serve as the primary liaison for referrals and joint case planning with clinical, treatment, housing, justice, and family\-service partners — including UCS Healthcare, ThriveNow Recovery Center, The Beacon, DART, Iowa HHS DCFS, family court, and Polk County corrections.
* Cultivate and maintain referral relationships to keep the program at capacity.

**Compliance, Data \& Reporting**

* Ensure strict adherence to all grant performance measures and Iowa HHS Opioid Settlement Funding contract requirements.
* Serve as the program's data steward: accurate, timely, and secure data entry and management in Airtable and FiveCRM, in full compliance with HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2\.
* Complete 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality training upon hire and annually thereafter, and ensure all staff with access to participant records do the same before handling protected substance use disorder information.
* Prepare and submit quarterly progress and outcome reports in IowaGrants and support monthly reimbursement claims.
* Monitor program fidelity benchmarks (housing stability, MOUD engagement, family reunification, voucher pacing) and trigger operational adjustments, partner consultation, and leadership reporting when thresholds are crossed.

**Housing Quality \& Program Integrity**

* Ensure voucher\-funded housing meets NARR certification standards and remains safe, stable, and recovery\-conducive.
* Uphold MOUD\-supportive, non\-discriminatory practice across all recovery pathways (MOUD, 12\-step, SMART Recovery, faith\-based, and holistic).

Qualifications

**Required**

* Bachelor's degree in social work, public administration, healthcare administration, counseling, public health, or a related behavioral health or human services field — **or** an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
* Minimum 2 years in a supervisory, coordinator, or program\-management role in behavioral health, family support, recovery services, social services, or a related field.
* Direct experience working with individuals or families affected by OUD, substance use disorders, or related behavioral health conditions.
* Experience with nonprofit financial oversight, grant compliance, data collection, or outcome reporting.
* Demonstrated ability to coordinate services across HHS, healthcare systems, community\-based partners, and family\-service systems.
* Strong organizational, communication, and documentation skills, with proficiency in data and case\-management systems.

**Preferred**

* A professional credential such as Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor (CADC), Certified Recovery Residence Admi

jobs.title: Director of Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
About AlphaHire Intelligence
AlphaHire is a Workforce Intelligence Platform serving the construction, infrastructure, energy, power, and mission\-critical markets.


We help senior executives, private equity partners, operating partners, investors, developers, contractors, and project leaders answer a critical question before committing capital:

**Can this project, investment, expansion, acquisition, or growth strategy actually be executed?**


Our intelligence supports decisions connected to projects and investments frequently valued at more than $100 million.


AlphaHire evaluates the workforce and market conditions that can determine whether those decisions succeed, including:

* Workforce availability and capacity
* Compensation pressure
* Hiring competition
* Skilled\-labor constraints
* Project pipeline activity
* Infrastructure and power constraints
* Market saturation
* Contractor capacity
* Geographic expansion readiness
* Leadership and workforce concentration risk


We provide workforce and market intelligence that helps executives reduce execution risk before making major capital, expansion, investment, and operating decisions.


This position is exclusively focused on developing commercial partnerships for **AlphaHire Intelligence products and executive decision\-support solutions**. It does not involve selling recruiting or staffing services.


Our Research Ecosystem
AlphaHire’s intelligence capabilities are supported by a growing research ecosystem that includes the **Workforce Intelligence Lab** and the **AlphaHire Research Library**.


The Workforce Intelligence Lab is our nonprofit research organization focused on advancing workforce intelligence through original research, publications, fellowships, academic collaboration, grants, and institutional partnerships.


Our research ecosystem collaborates with multiple universities, academic faculty, research scientists, industry experts, and analytical partners. Research areas include:

* Workforce economics
* Labor\-market forecasting
* Infrastructure workforce capacity
* Compensation intelligence
* Labor shortages and hiring competition
* Construction workforce trends
* Workforce planning and execution risk


The AlphaHire Research Library brings together workforce studies, market intelligence, executive briefings, data, white papers, and industry research designed to support better executive decisions.


The Opportunity
AlphaHire is seeking a Director of Strategic Partnerships to build commercial relationships that expand the reach, distribution, and adoption of AlphaHire Intelligence across the United States.


You will identify organizations that already advise, influence, convene, or provide services to AlphaHire’s target buyers. These relationships may include referral partnerships, co\-selling arrangements, channel relationships, commercial research collaborations, data partnerships, enterprise distribution opportunities, and other revenue\-producing alliances.


Potential partners may include:

* Management consulting and advisory firms
* Private equity service\-provider networks
* Infrastructure and investment organizations
* Engineering, EPC, and professional\-services firms
* Construction and industry associations
* Economic\-development and site\-selection organizations
* Enterprise technology and data providers
* Research and market\-intelligence platforms
* Utilities, developers, and major project ecosystems
* Professional and institutional networks


Customer engagements produced through these partnerships typically range from approximately **$50,000 to $250,000** in first\-year contract value.

 **Requirements**  

* Identify and prioritize organizations capable of introducing, distributing, recommending, or co\-selling AlphaHire Intelligence.
* Develop relationships with senior executives, managing directors, partners, practice leaders, association leaders, and ecosystem decision\-makers.
* Build the strategic and commercial case for partnering with AlphaHire.
* Determine the appropriate partnership model, including referral, co\-selling, channel, distribution, research, data, or enterprise\-access arrangements.
* Lead initial partnership conversations and executive discovery.
* Qualify each organization’s buyer access, market credibility, commercial alignment, and revenue potential.
* Develop partnership proposals and activation plans with AlphaHire leadership.
* Negotiate commercial terms within approved parameters.
* Establish clear account ownership, referral attribution, opportunity\-registration, and communication processes.
* Convert partnership agreements into active introductions, qualified opportunities, and collected revenue.
* Coordinate partner\-enabled executive briefings, demonstrations, events, research discussions, and market initiatives.
* Maintain accurate records of partner activity, introductions, opportunities, and revenue.
* Monitor partnership performance and prioritize relationships producing measurable commercial outcomes.
* Represent AlphaHire accurately using approved positioning, research, and commercial materials.

  

**Benefits**  

This opportunity may be a strong fit if you have previously worked as a:

* Director of Strategic Partnerships
* Strategic Partnerships Executive
* Alliances Director
* Channel Sales Director
* Partner Development Director
* Ecosystem Partnerships Director
* Business Development Director
* Client Partner
* Managing Director
* Industry or Practice Leader


We are most interested in the partnerships you have personally originated, the executive relationships you can credibly activate, and the revenue those partnerships produced.


Successful candidates will understand that a partnership is valuable only when it creates measurable access, qualified opportunities, strategic distribution, or commercial revenue.


AlphaHire provides equal consideration to qualified applicants and contractors without regard to legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Bleeding Disorders Assn of NENY
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

BDANENY is seeking a versatile, strategic, and hands\-on **Executive Director (ED)** to lead our chapter. As the chief executive officer, you will wear many hats—acting as both the strategic visionary and the operational anchor for the organization. You will oversee everything from high\-level advocacy and coalition building to day\-to\-day office administration, financial oversight, fundraising, and member support.

The ideal candidate is an empathetic leader with a sharp business mind, a passion for healthcare advocacy, and the ability to comfortably pivot between community engagement and rigorous non\-profit compliance.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Office Administration \& Financial Oversight**

* **Daily Operations:** Manage tech infrastructure, equipment, supplies, and database maintenance (Bloomerang). Oversee essential apps and programs (Zoom, Microsoft Office, MailChimp, Namecheap, etc.).
* **Financial Management:** Handle payroll, bill paying, and meticulous budgeting.
* **Compliance \& Banking:** Provide oversight for banking and financial services (Key Bank, credit card processing). Ensure full compliance with the IRS, NYS, and the NYS Charities Bureau.
* **Insurance \& HR Risk:** Manage Workers' Compensation, disability, and Directors and Officers (D\&O) insurance policies.

**2\. Fundraising \& Development**

* **Event Planning:** Direct major annual fundraising initiatives, most notably the signature BDANENY Walk.
* **Grant Management:** Write, submit, and report on organizational and program\-specific grants.
* **Vendor \& Corporate Relations:** Manage industry vendor relationships, including pharmaceutical and specialty pharmacy portals and formal letters of request.

**3\. Advocacy \& Policy Tracking**

* **Coalition \& Government Relations:** Represent BDANENY in the NYS Bleeding Disorders Coalition; meet with government officials, write advocacy letters, and champion bills of interest.
* **Policy Monitoring:** Stay current on federal and state policies, programs, and pending legislation (including CDC, NIH, CMS, SSA, and Medicaid).
* **Care Barrier Identification:** Actively identify and address impediments to patient care, including inpatient issues, Medicare/Medicaid hurdles, and commercial insurance barriers.

**4\. Member Support \& Community Education**

* **Direct Aid Programs:** Oversee the administration of member support initiatives, including BDA Grants, emergency funds, travel reimbursements, scholarships, and MedicAlert bracelets.
* **Educational Programming:** Plan and execute sponsored dinners, webinars, and the BDANENY Annual Meeting.

**5\. Marketing, Communications \& Design**

* **Digital Presence:** Maintain the organization's website, including technical backend tasks (domains, SSL certificates, and Cloudflare).
* **Public Relations:** Drive community engagement via Facebook, MailChimp newsletters, and internal graphic design needs for promotional materials.

**6\. Coalition Building \& Meetings Management**

* **Strategic Partnerships:** Foster vital relationships with regional and national partners, including but not limited to Medicaid Matters, the Chapter \& Staff Organization (CSO), HFA, NBDF, the Red Cross, Rensselaer County Chamber of Commerce, Troy BID, Stewart’s, Double H Ranch, and Sickle Cell/other disease state associations.
* **Stakeholder Meetings:** Manage communications and logistics for the Board of Directors, organizational committees, Hemophilia Treatment Centers (HTCs), and corporate vendors.

**Qualifications**

* **Experience:** 5\+ years of progressive leadership experience in non\-profit management, healthcare administration, or a relevant sector preferred.
* **Technical \& Financial Acumen:** Proven experience managing payroll, budgets, NYS compliance (Charities Bureau), and fundamental IT/database systems (Bloomerang, MailChimp, Cloudflare/web domains).
* **Advocacy \& Healthcare Knowledge:** Strong understanding of New York State legislative processes, Medicaid, and the healthcare barriers facing rare disease communities.
* **Fundraising Prowess:** Demonstrated success in grant writing, event logistics (Walks), and corporate vendor relations.
* **Design \& Communication:** Basic graphic design capability and excellent written communication skills for newsletters, letter\-writing campaigns, and digital media.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Business, Public Administration, Public Health, Non\-Profit Management) preferred

**About Us**

The Bleeding Disorders Association of Northeastern New York (BDANENY) is a dedicated non\-profit organization serving individuals and families affected by hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, and other rare bleeding disorders. Our mission is to improve the quality of life for our community through advocacy, education, support, and research funding. We provide a vital network of resources and a compassionate community for those navigating these lifelong conditions.

**To Apply**

Interested candidates should submit a thoughtful **cover letter** detailing their alignment with our mission and operational needs, along with a **current resume** to memberservices@bdaneny.org with the subject line "Executive Director Application – \[Your Name]".

*BDANENY is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and community members.*

Pay: $60,000\.00 \- $70,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Troy, NY 12180

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
**General Purpose**
The Chief Operating Officer oversees the day\-to\-day administrative and operational functions of the organization. This role is responsible for translating strategic plans into actionable initiatives, optimizing processes across all departments, and ensuring operational efficiency and effectiveness in achieving business goals. The COO works closely with the CEO and executive leadership team to drive organizational performance, growth, and compliance.

 **Responsibilities****Operational Leadership \& Strategy**

* Implement and manage operational strategies that align with the organization’s mission, vision, and objectives.
* Translate strategic initiatives into actionable plans across multiple departments and facilities.
* Collaborate with the CEO and executive leadership team to develop long\-term business plans and growth strategies.
**Departmental Oversight \& Efficiency**

* Oversee daily operations of all organizational departments, including clinical, administrative, HR, IT, finance, marketing, and customer service.
* Establish and monitor key operational metrics and performance goals to ensure accountability and efficiency.
* Identify opportunities to streamline processes, improve workflows, and optimize resource utilization.
**Leadership \& Team Development**

* Lead cross\-functional teams and initiatives to enhance organizational effectiveness.
* Recruit, train, mentor, and evaluate operational leadership across departments.
* Foster a culture of collaboration, continuous improvement, and high performance.
**Policy, Compliance \& Risk Management**

* Develop, implement, and enforce policies and procedures that support operational excellence and regulatory compliance.
* Identify operational risks and implement mitigation strategies to ensure continuity and minimize disruptions.
* Ensure all departments adhere to applicable state, federal, and industry regulations, including healthcare compliance standards for skilled nursing facilities.
**Financial \& Resource Management**

* Manage departmental budgets, staffing plans, and resource allocation in collaboration with the CFO and department heads.
* Monitor operational expenditures and identify cost\-saving opportunities without compromising quality.
**Communication \& Reporting**

* Serve as a liaison between departments, ensuring clear communication, alignment, and collaboration toward organizational goals.
* Prepare and present operational performance reports, metrics, and milestones to the CEO and board of directors.
* Relay changes in processes, priorities, or strategies to appropriate teams and stakeholders.
**Additional Responsibilities**

* Participate in executive leadership discussions, decision\-making, and strategic planning.
* Perform other duties as assigned by the CEO or board of directors.
**Qualifications*** Proven executive leadership experience, preferably in healthcare or skilled nursing facility operations.
* Strong operational management, analytical, and problem\-solving skills.
* Excellent communication, interpersonal, and team\-building abilities.
* Knowledge of regulatory and compliance requirements related to healthcare operations.
* Demonstrated ability to implement process improvements and manage large, complex organizations. Regular and reliable attendance is required to perform the essential functions of this position.

Position Type: Full\-Time, Exempt

Reports To: Board of Directors

Location: Chelan, Washington On\-site Role

**Organization \& Facility Profile:** 

Lake Chelan Community Center is a vital anchor for our community, operating out of a premier 44,000\-square\-foot multi\-use facility. Our campus features a regulation gymnasium, performing arts center, short\- and long\-term commercial/non\-profit office space rentals, and multi\-purpose conference and event spaces. We blend accessible community programming with a robust asset\-rental model to ensure long\-term community impact and financial sustainability. Position Summary The Executive Director serves as the Chief Executive Officer and operations leader of the center. This role requires a unique blend of visionary non\-profit leadership and sharp commercial business acumen. The Executive Director is responsible for maximizing community programming, driving earned income through strategic space and asset rentals, and managing a complex facility budget.

**To apply, please send your resume and a cover letter to hello@chelancommunity.org**

**Key Responsibilities**

Facility Asset Management \& Revenue Generation

* Earned Revenue Strategy: Maximize the utilization and financial return of the center’s physical assets, including corporate rentals for the conference center and booking external productions/performers for the performing arts center.
* Tenant Relations: Oversee the leasing and management of the on\-site office spaces, ensuring high occupancy rates, positive tenant relations, and lease compliance.
* Athletic \& Recreation Oversight: Guide the management of the gymnasium, balancing profitable tournament/league rentals with accessible community open\-gym and youth sports programs.
* Vendor \& Contractor Management: Supervise third\-party vendors for facility maintenance, HVAC, security, janitorial services, and specialized theatrical/AV production teams.

Fundraising \& Fiscal Leadership

* Diversified Funding: Balance earned income with a robust philanthropic portfolio, including individual major donors, corporate sponsorships, and government/foundation grants.
* Capital \& Operations Budgeting: Formulate and manage an annual operating budget that accounts for heavy facility overhead, capital replacement reserves (sinking funds), and program expenses.

Programming \& Creative Vision

* Arts \& Culture Cultivation: Collaborate with artistic staff and partners to curate diverse, culturally rich programming for the performing arts center that serves the local community.
* Inclusive Programming: Ensure the gymnasium and event spaces host equitable programming that addresses local health, wellness, and social needs.

Team Leadership \& Governance

* Multi\-Disciplinary Team Management: Hire, mentor, and lead a diverse staff across distinct departments (including Facilities/Operations, Arts Programming, Athletics, Events/Hospitality, and Fundraising).
* Board Collaboration: Work directly with the Board of Directors to execute the strategic plan, provide transparent financial reporting, and support board development sub\-committees. 103 Bighorn Way, Chelan, WA 98816 www.chelancommunity.org @chelancommunity

Marketing \& Communications

* Marketing Strategy: Develop and implement a comprehensive marketing strategy to increase community awareness and participation. Coordinate promotional campaigns for events and fundraising activities. Identify opportunities to enhance the Community Center’s visibility and reputation within the community and region.
* Brand Support: Maintain branding standards to ensure consistent representation of the Community Center across all platforms and materials. Continue to build a strong brand that advances the Community Center’s mission and supports growth objectives.
* Communications: Serve as the primary spokesperson and public representative of the Community Center, cultivating positive relationships with community members, media, partners and stakeholders. Manage the website, social media platforms, and other communication channels to ensure consistent messaging and brand identity.

Human Resources/Personnel

* Oversight: Provide strategic leadership and oversight for all human resources functions, including recruitment, hiring, onboarding, employee relations, and staff development. Recruit, hire, and supervise staff to ensure a high\-performing and mission\-driven workforce. Oversee volunteer screening and training where applicable.
* Employee Performance: Oversee employee performance management processes, including goal setting, coaching, evaluations, and corrective action when necessary.
* Records \& Safety: Maintain accurate personnel records and ensure compliance with employment, safety, and labor regulations. Promote workplace safety and risk management practices to protect employees, volunteers, participants, and organizational assets.

Qualifications

* Experience: 7\+ years of progressive senior leadership experience. Direct experience managing multi\-use facilities, community centers, public venues, or hospitality/property management assets is highly preferred.
* Business \& Real Estate Savvy: Proven track record in lease negotiation, property management, or large\-scale event space/theater booking.
* Financial Acumen: Deep experience managing complex operational budgets ($1M\+ preferred) with multiple revenue streams (earned income \+ philanthropic giving).
* Technical Familiarity: Understanding of facility management software, venue booking systems (e.g., Event Temple, Tripleseat), and standard non\-profit CRM tools.

Education: Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s in Non\-Profit Management, Business Administration (MBA), or Public Administration (MPA) preferred.

Pay: $100,000\.00 \- $110,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible spending account

Work Location: In person

**Job Title:** Senior Director of Operations \& Support Services  
**Location:** Christian City, GA  
**Department:** Support Services  
**Reports To:** Chief Operating Officer (COO)  
**FLSA Status:** Exempt, Full Time

**About Christian City**

Christian City is a faith\-based, nonprofit organization located in Union City, Georgia, serving children, families, and older adults for over 60 years. Situated on a 500\-acre campus, Christian City provides a continuum of care through residential programs for children and youth, foster care and family services, transitional living for young adults, and active senior living.

Rooted in compassion and community, Christian City is committed to creating a safe, supportive, and purpose\-driven environment where individuals can heal, grow, and thrive.

**Position Summary**

The Sr. Director of Operations \& Support Services provides strategic leadership and operational oversight of key support functions across Christian City. This role works collaboratively across all departments to ensure campus operations are efficient, safe, and well\-coordinated. The Director is responsible for Campus Patrol, fleet management, coordination of renovations, oversight of Facility Maintenance Team for scheduled and unscheduled building maintenance, budget and forecast management, schedule synchronization, and project management. This position plays a critical role in aligning operational priorities with organizational goals while supporting residents, staff, and leadership.

**Essential Duties \& Responsibilities**

**Fleet Management**

* Oversee all aspects of organizational vehicle operations, policies, and procedures.
* Monitor vehicle maintenance schedules and coordinate routine and preventative servicing of our 13 vehicle fleet.
* Track vehicle usage, mileage, registrations, and insurance documentation.
* Prepare and present monthly fleet utilization and maintenance reports.
* Ensure compliance with safety standards and regulatory requirements.

**Renovation \& Facilities Coordination**

* Coordinate residential unit renovations and campus facility improvements.
* Work closely across all departments to align renovation timelines with operational and program needs.
* Oversee contractors performing upgrades, repairs, and capital improvement projects.
* Ensure projects are completed on time, within scope, and in compliance with safety and quality standards.
* Prioritize and coordinate daily work schedule for 5\-person facility maintenance team.

**Campus Patrol**

* Supervise Campus Patrol operations and scheduling of 7\-person Team
* Supervise development and implementation of Campus Risk Management and Emergency Response Plan
* Ensure adequate coverage and efficient allocation of resources.

**Budget \& Forecast Management**

* Develop and manage operating budgets for Support Services functions.
* Monitor expenses, analyze trends, and prepare forecasts to support leadership decision\-making.
* Identify cost efficiencies and resource optimization opportunities.
* Provide regular financial updates and variance reports to the COO.

**Scheduling \& Operational Synchronization**

* Coordinate work schedules across Support Services, Maintenance, Campus Patrol, and related operational teams.
* Work across all departments to ensure schedules are aligned with campus priorities, events, and staffing needs to ensure adequate coverage and efficient allocation of resources.

**Project Management**

* Lead operational and cross\-functional projects that support campus operations and long\-term improvements.
* Develop project plans, timelines, and deliverables while monitoring progress and milestones.
* Communicate project updates, risks, and outcomes to leadership and stakeholders.
* Proactively address challenges to maintain project momentum.
* Assist COO in planning and synchronization of campus\-level initiatives and major construction projects.

**Maintenance Oversight**

* Provide leadership and direction to the Maintenance Supervisor and assigned team members.
* Establish maintenance priorities and oversee preventive and corrective maintenance activities.
* Ensure timely ordering and availability of tools, equipment, and supplies.
* Review daily, weekly, and monthly maintenance reports to monitor productivity and service quality.

**Contract Oversight**

* Manage and oversee vendor and contractor relationships supporting campus operations.
* Coordinate contracts related to fire suppression and monitoring, safety and security systems, residential unit renovations, major repairs, landscaping, and grounds maintenance.
* Monitor contractor performance to ensure compliance with contract terms, safety standards, and service expectations.
* Review invoices and recommend approval in alignment with budget and contractual agreements.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience considered.
* Demonstrated experience in facilities management, project management, or operational leadership.
* Strong management and people\-leadership skills with experience supervising teams.
* Proven project management capabilities, including managing multiple priorities and timelines.
* Excellent organizational, communication, and problem\-solving skills.
* Experience with formal planning processes including Lean Six Sigma or MDMP.
* Ability to adjust work priorities based on changing circumstances.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and maintenance management systems; WorxHub experience preferred.
* Valid driver’s license with a clean driving record.

**Physical Requirements**

* Ability to stand, walk, and sit for extended periods.
* Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds as needed.
* Ability to work in both indoor and outdoor environments.

**Management Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises operational supervisors and support staff.
* Provides oversight for multiple teams across campus operations.

jobs.title: Director of Partnerships
jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

  


DREAM seeks a relationship\-driven, strategic, and collaborative **Director of Partnerships** to lead the development and stewardship of partnerships that support DREAM’s growth, programming, and long\-term sustainability.

  

DREAM relies on partnerships with affordable housing communities, housing authorities, schools, and other community\-based organizations to enter new communities and sustain our work over time. As DREAM continues to grow, partnerships beyond our core program sites are also becoming increasingly important to our operations, including relationships with summer meal providers, pools and parks, literacy organizations, camps, enrichment providers, and other community resources.



The Director of Partnerships will develop and implement a comprehensive partnership strategy across DREAM’s regions and programs. This position will cultivate relationships with affordable housing networks and management organizations, identify prospective program sites, steward existing partners, oversee partnership agreements, and help regional teams build strong and sustainable community connections.



The role will support partnership development for both DREAM’s Village Mentoring and Guided Mentoring programs while also building broader partnerships that expand opportunities and resources for young people. The ideal candidate has experience in affordable housing, community development, partnership management, or a related field and understands how to translate relationships into measurable organizational growth and impact.

 **Essential Functions**

  


Partnership Strategy and Growth


* Develop and implement an organization\-wide partnership strategy aligned with DREAM’s mission, programs, and growth goals.
* Create regional growth maps and conduct outreach to prospective partners in current and emerging regions.
* Establish annual partnership goals and track progress toward growth, stewardship, and renewal targets.
* Identify trends, gaps, and opportunities that inform DREAM’s regional and organizational growth strategy.


Housing and Program Partnerships


* Build and steward relationships with housing authorities, affordable housing organizations, property managers, schools, and community\-based organizations.
* Cultivate new partners that can support the expansion of DREAM’s Village Mentoring and Guided Mentoring programs.
* Represent DREAM within housing, education, community development, and nonprofit networks.
* Work with regional and program staff to assess prospective partners and determine readiness for new programming.


Partner Stewardship and Agreements


* Maintain strong relationships with existing partners through regular communication, recognition, reporting, and opportunities for feedback.
* Coordinate partner check\-ins, renewals, and follow\-up while supporting regional teams in navigating relationship challenges.
* Oversee the creation, execution, organization, and renewal of contracts, memoranda of understanding, and site agreements.
* Maintain centralized systems for tracking partnership contacts, commitments, agreements, deadlines, and next steps.


Community Resource Partnerships


* Develop partnerships that expand resources and opportunities for DREAM programs and youth, including summer meals, literacy programs, pools, parks, camps, transportation, and enrichment providers.
* Identify donated, discounted, or shared resources that strengthen programming and reduce costs.
* Help regional teams identify and cultivate local resource partners.


Collaboration and Reporting


* Serve as an organizational resource and provide tools, guidance, and training related to partnership development and stewardship.
* Collaborate with program, development, finance, communications, and regional teams to align partnership activities with organizational priorities.
* Maintain partnership records, prepare regular updates, and evaluate the effectiveness of DREAM’s partnership strategy.


**Qualifications**


* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience.
* Two or more years of relevant experience in partnerships, affordable housing, community development, external relations, business development, or nonprofit leadership.
* Demonstrated success developing and sustaining external partnerships.
* Experience in affordable housing, including work with housing authorities, property management organizations, developers, resident services, or housing networks, strongly preferred.
* Experience developing partnership, outreach, or organizational growth strategies.
* Experience managing contracts, memoranda of understanding, or partnership agreements.
* Strong relationship\-building, communication, presentation, project\-management, and organizational skills.
* Ability to balance strategic planning with consistent follow\-through, documentation, and day\-to\-day relationship management.
* Experience working across multiple regions or with youth\-serving and community\-based programs preferred.
* Ability to travel periodically to DREAM regions and partner communities.


**Core Competencies**


* Relationship building and stakeholder engagement
* Partnership development and stewardship
* Strategic thinking and growth planning
* Knowledge of affordable housing and community systems
* Project management and follow\-through
* Cross\-functional collaboration
* Communication and problem\-solving
* Cultural humility and commitment to equitable community partnership


**Compensation**



Compensation for this position is based on experience, qualifications, and level of responsibility. DREAM is committed to internal equity and recognizes that candidates may bring varying levels of relevant expertise.



The anticipated salary range for this position is approximately $50,000–$70,000 annually, along with a comprehensive benefits package.

 **About DREAM**



DREAM partners with youth and families living in affordable housing communities to close the opportunity

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Bleeding Disorders Assn of NENY
new_jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

BDANENY is seeking a versatile, strategic, and hands\-on **Executive Director (ED)** to lead our chapter. As the chief executive officer, you will wear many hats—acting as both the strategic visionary and the operational anchor for the organization. You will oversee everything from high\-level advocacy and coalition building to day\-to\-day office administration, financial oversight, fundraising, and member support.

The ideal candidate is an empathetic leader with a sharp business mind, a passion for healthcare advocacy, and the ability to comfortably pivot between community engagement and rigorous non\-profit compliance.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1\. Office Administration \& Financial Oversight**

* **Daily Operations:** Manage tech infrastructure, equipment, supplies, and database maintenance (Bloomerang). Oversee essential apps and programs (Zoom, Microsoft Office, MailChimp, Namecheap, etc.).
* **Financial Management:** Handle payroll, bill paying, and meticulous budgeting.
* **Compliance \& Banking:** Provide oversight for banking and financial services (Key Bank, credit card processing). Ensure full compliance with the IRS, NYS, and the NYS Charities Bureau.
* **Insurance \& HR Risk:** Manage Workers' Compensation, disability, and Directors and Officers (D\&O) insurance policies.

**2\. Fundraising \& Development**

* **Event Planning:** Direct major annual fundraising initiatives, most notably the signature BDANENY Walk.
* **Grant Management:** Write, submit, and report on organizational and program\-specific grants.
* **Vendor \& Corporate Relations:** Manage industry vendor relationships, including pharmaceutical and specialty pharmacy portals and formal letters of request.

**3\. Advocacy \& Policy Tracking**

* **Coalition \& Government Relations:** Represent BDANENY in the NYS Bleeding Disorders Coalition; meet with government officials, write advocacy letters, and champion bills of interest.
* **Policy Monitoring:** Stay current on federal and state policies, programs, and pending legislation (including CDC, NIH, CMS, SSA, and Medicaid).
* **Care Barrier Identification:** Actively identify and address impediments to patient care, including inpatient issues, Medicare/Medicaid hurdles, and commercial insurance barriers.

**4\. Member Support \& Community Education**

* **Direct Aid Programs:** Oversee the administration of member support initiatives, including BDA Grants, emergency funds, travel reimbursements, scholarships, and MedicAlert bracelets.
* **Educational Programming:** Plan and execute sponsored dinners, webinars, and the BDANENY Annual Meeting.

**5\. Marketing, Communications \& Design**

* **Digital Presence:** Maintain the organization's website, including technical backend tasks (domains, SSL certificates, and Cloudflare).
* **Public Relations:** Drive community engagement via Facebook, MailChimp newsletters, and internal graphic design needs for promotional materials.

**6\. Coalition Building \& Meetings Management**

* **Strategic Partnerships:** Foster vital relationships with regional and national partners, including but not limited to Medicaid Matters, the Chapter \& Staff Organization (CSO), HFA, NBDF, the Red Cross, Rensselaer County Chamber of Commerce, Troy BID, Stewart’s, Double H Ranch, and Sickle Cell/other disease state associations.
* **Stakeholder Meetings:** Manage communications and logistics for the Board of Directors, organizational committees, Hemophilia Treatment Centers (HTCs), and corporate vendors.

**Qualifications**

* **Experience:** 5\+ years of progressive leadership experience in non\-profit management, healthcare administration, or a relevant sector preferred.
* **Technical \& Financial Acumen:** Proven experience managing payroll, budgets, NYS compliance (Charities Bureau), and fundamental IT/database systems (Bloomerang, MailChimp, Cloudflare/web domains).
* **Advocacy \& Healthcare Knowledge:** Strong understanding of New York State legislative processes, Medicaid, and the healthcare barriers facing rare disease communities.
* **Fundraising Prowess:** Demonstrated success in grant writing, event logistics (Walks), and corporate vendor relations.
* **Design \& Communication:** Basic graphic design capability and excellent written communication skills for newsletters, letter\-writing campaigns, and digital media.

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (Business, Public Administration, Public Health, Non\-Profit Management) preferred

**About Us**

The Bleeding Disorders Association of Northeastern New York (BDANENY) is a dedicated non\-profit organization serving individuals and families affected by hemophilia, von Willebrand disease, and other rare bleeding disorders. Our mission is to improve the quality of life for our community through advocacy, education, support, and research funding. We provide a vital network of resources and a compassionate community for those navigating these lifelong conditions.

**To Apply**

Interested candidates should submit a thoughtful **cover letter** detailing their alignment with our mission and operational needs, along with a **current resume** to memberservices@bdaneny.org with the subject line "Executive Director Application – \[Your Name]".

*BDANENY is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and community members.*

Pay: $60,000\.00 \- $70,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Troy, NY 12180
